top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a specific, instrument-driven invention (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) realised at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty by Ye's strontium systems and reproduced independently at JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB and SYRTE. The two names map onto concept and record realisation, and the citation can be worded around the lattice clock so it is distinct from the 1989, 2005 and 2012 prizes. It is more mature and more cleanly attributed than the twisted bilayer graphene proposal, whose pairing mechanism is unsettled and which leaves out Yuan Cao; P002 is a credible second choice and is still preferred to no award.
